transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for fitting me in. Um... I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need. I'm just here because... well, mostly I just don't feel like myself anymore. It's probably just a slump, nothing too terrible, but... I used to do a lot of things. I'd go hiking, I was coaching, playing my guitar... but I just kind of stopped. 

I haven't even been calling people back, which I feel really terrible about. I know it's not polite, and I don't want people to think I don't care. And, um... I'm a little embarrassed to admit this part, but some days I just sit in my small rental for hours. I know there are things I should be doing, and I really want to be productive, but I just... I can't seem to make myself start. 

Is that... does that make sense to you? I hope I'm explaining it okay. I just want to get back to being a good, reliable guy, you know?
Do you still enjoy the activities you used to do, like hiking, coaching, or playing your guitar, when you do manage to do them?

Um... I wish I could give you a better answer, but... I guess I don't really know? I haven't actually managed to do any of them lately to find out. 

I know I should just force myself to get out there, and I feel really bad that I haven't. I don't want you to think I'm just lazy or giving up, because I'm usually a really active guy. But I haven't even taken my guitar out of the case in... well, a long time. So I'm not sure if it would still feel good or not. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be trying harder. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
Do you find pleasure in anything at all lately?

I... I really wish I could give you a better answer. I want to be optimistic for you, I really do. But honestly... like I was saying before, I just don't feel like myself anymore. Since I stopped doing all my normal stuff—the hiking, the coaching, the guitar—there just hasn't been much... joy, I guess? 

Even when I'm just sitting in my rental for hours, I'll think about things I could do, things I know I *should* be doing, but... I just can't make myself start them. So, I guess the answer is no, I haven't really found pleasure in anything lately. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds really negative, and I promise I'm usually a much more upbeat guy. I hate sounding like I'm just complaining. Is it okay that I don't have a better answer for you right now?
Have you been feeling sad most of the time lately?

Um... well, no, not exactly sad. I know it probably sounds like I should be sad, since I'm not doing my usual stuff... but I'm not sitting around crying or feeling miserable or anything like that. 

It's more like... I just don't feel much of anything at all. Just kind of... blank, I guess? 

I hope that's a helpful answer. I don't want to give you the wrong impression, and I'm really trying to be as accurate as I can for you so you can do your job. Does that make sense, though? Not really being sad, but just sort of... empty?
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

I feel like I'm repeating myself a bit, and I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the specific details you need. But... yeah, I guess I have lost interest. 

Like I mentioned before, I just don't really feel like myself anymore. I completely stopped doing all the things I used to love—the hiking, coaching the kids, playing my guitar. I don't even call people back anymore, which I feel terrible about because I don't want my friends to think I don't care about them. 

Some days, I just sit in my little rental house for hours. I know there are things I should be doing, and I tell myself to get up and do them, but... I just can't seem to make myself start. 

I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record or coming across as lazy. I'm trying my best to explain it right... is this the kind of information you're looking for?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. I really hope I haven't let it go on too long before getting help, I know doctors prefer when you catch things early. 

It kind of started... things just sort of started unraveling after my divorce. I had to move into this smaller rental house, and... well, that was about a year and two months ago. So I guess it's been going on since then. 

I'm sorry, I should have probably reached out sooner, shouldn't I? I just kept thinking I'd bounce back, you know? I really try to be a resilient person. I hope it's okay that I waited this long to talk to someone about it.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Um... no, I don't think so. Not that I've noticed, anyway. My uniforms and regular clothes still fit about the same as they usually do. 

I really try to make sure I'm still eating, even when I don't feel like doing much else. I know sometimes people stop taking care of themselves when they get in a slump, but I'm trying to be good about that so I don't cause any extra health problems for anyone to worry about. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, I hope it's okay that my weight has stayed pretty steady. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling restless or sluggish lately?

Um... no, I don't think I've been feeling restless. I'm not jittery or pacing around or anything like that. 

And sluggish... well, I know I said earlier that I sit around a lot, but my body doesn't actually feel slow or heavy. It's really just the getting started part that's hard for me. Once I'm actually up, I move around just fine. I really try to maintain my physical fitness, especially because of my line of work... I definitely don't want to just let myself go or be a burden to my team. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses for sitting around so much. I'm really trying my best to keep it together physically. Does that answer your question okay? I want to make sure I'm explaining the difference right.
Do you often feel guilty about things you've done or haven't done?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I feel guilty. I mean, I try really hard to do things by the book, especially at work. In my line of work, you really have to be dependable and follow protocol, so I always make sure I'm doing exactly what I'm supposed to do. I never want to let my team down or make a mistake that hurts somebody. 

So, because I try to be so careful, I don't really have a lot of guilt weighing on me. I hope that doesn't make me sound arrogant? Like I think I'm perfect or something, because I definitely know I'm not. I just... I really try to be a good person and do what's expected of me so I don't cause problems for anyone else. 

Is that... does that make sense for what you're asking? I hope I'm answering that right.
Do you often feel worthless or like you're not a good person?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't feel worthless. I know I have a purpose, especially with my job. Being in protective services, you know, people rely on you to be strong and capable, and I take that responsibility really seriously. I try to be someone people can count on. 

I really try to be a good person, too. I try to treat people with respect and do the right thing, even when it's hard. I don't want to be a burden or a bad influence on anyone. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm bragging? I just... I try to focus on the positive things I can contribute, you know? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I see myself. Does that sound okay?
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I haven't had any thoughts like that at all. 

Um... like I was saying about my job, being in protective services, my whole purpose is to keep people safe. I take that really, really seriously. I would never want to do anything to hurt myself and... well, leave my team short-handed or make anyone worry about me. I would hate to cause that kind of stress for anyone.

I really try to keep my head on straight and stay safe, you know? I want to make sure I'm doing everything right for my health so I can keep being a reliable guy for the people who need me. 

I hope that's reassuring? I just want you to know you absolutely don't have to worry about me doing anything like that. Did I explain that okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.
Have you been experiencing these feelings of emptiness and disinterest in activities most of the day, nearly every day?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I wouldn't say I'm completely empty, that sounds so... so dramatic, you know? I just... I haven't quite been feeling like myself lately. 

I used to do a lot of things. I'd go hiking, I was coaching, I'd play my guitar... and I was always pretty good about calling people back. But lately, I've kind of stopped doing all that. I've just been staying in my small rental place. Sometimes I'll just sit there for hours. I know there are things I should be doing, like chores or errands, but I just... I can't seem to make myself start them. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy? I really am a hard worker, I promise. It's just been a bit of a slump, I think. Everyone gets into slumps sometimes, right? I'm sure I'll bounce back soon and get back to my normal routine. 

Does that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
For how long have you lost interest in the activities you used to enjoy, such as hiking, coaching, or playing your guitar?

Um... well, it hasn't been that long, really. Maybe just a few weeks? Or a month or so? It's hard to put an exact timeline on it. 

I really don't want you to think this is a permanent thing. Like I said, I usually have a lot of energy and I'm very involved in things. It's just... lately, with work being so demanding, I think I've just needed some extra downtime to recharge. That's totally normal for someone in my line of work, isn't it? You have to make sure you're rested so you can be alert on the job. 

So, yeah, it's just been a recent thing, just taking a little break from all the extra stuff. I'm sure I'll be picking up my guitar again any day now. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure you understand that I'm usually a very active guy.
How long have you felt like you've lost interest in the things you used to enjoy?

Well, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, and really thinking about it... it might be a bit longer than a few weeks. 

I just... I didn't want it to sound like I've been neglecting things for a long time, because I really do try to stay on top of everything. But, um, things have kind of been... unraveling, I guess you could say, since I moved into this smaller rental place. That was after my divorce, which was... gosh, about a year and two months ago now. 

It's just been a lot of adjustment, you know? Downsizing, getting used to a new routine on my own... I think it just took more out of me than I realized. But I'm really trying my best to get back on track. I don't want you to think I've just given up for a whole year. It's just been a slow process of getting settled. 

Does that... is that an okay answer? I just want to be as helpful as I can, even if it's a little embarrassing to admit it's been going on for that long.
Has your lack of interest in activities like hiking, coaching, or playing your guitar lasted for more than two months?

Yes, um... like I was just mentioning, I guess it really has been. It's, well, it's been about a year and two months. Ever since I moved into the smaller rental after my divorce. 

So, yes, definitely more than two months. I... I really apologize if I made it confusing earlier when I said a few weeks. I just didn't want you to think I've been slacking off for over a year, you know? In my line of work, people really rely on you, and I pride myself on being dependable. It's just that things have kind of been unraveling since that move, and it's been hard to keep up with the extra stuff like the guitar or coaching. 

I'm really trying my best to get back to my old self, I promise. Am I... am I giving you the right information now? I want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you need.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the time lately?

Oh, no, no. I wouldn't say sad. Or depressed, definitely not. I mean... I know I just told you about not keeping up with my hobbies and how things unraveled a bit, but it's not because I'm sitting around crying or feeling down in the dumps. 

I'm a pretty resilient guy. You kind of have to be in my line of work, right? You can't let things get to you too much or you wouldn't be able to do the job. It's really just been more about feeling worn out from the move and the adjustment, not sadness. Mentally, I'm still keeping my chin up and pushing forward. 

I hope that's a good sign? I just don't want you to worry that I'm, you know, falling apart emotionally or anything like that. I'm doing okay in that department, I promise.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that normally would bring you joy?

Well, um... I guess "unable" sounds a little... severe? I don't want to make it sound like I'm completely broken or anything. But... if I'm really looking at it, mostly I just don't feel like myself anymore. 

Like I mentioned, I stopped the hiking, and the coaching... playing my guitar. I've even stopped calling people back, which really isn't like me at all. I'm usually the guy everyone can count on, you know? It's a bit embarrassing to admit this to you, but... some days I just sit in that small rental for hours. I know there are things I need to do, things I should be doing, but I just can't seem to make myself start. 

It's not that I don't want to enjoy things, it's just... a block, I guess? I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy to you. I'm usually a very hard worker, I swear. Does that answer what you were asking me?
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities is a major problem for you?

Well, I... I don't know if I'd call it a major problem, exactly. I mean, it's not ideal, obviously. But... well, I guess it has affected some things. 

It's just... well, I haven't been working lately. I'm a protective service worker, usually, and I... I had a bit of an incident on a routine patrol. I guess I startled some of the staff and the bystanders, and... well, they suspended me. I know it sounds bad, but it was just a misunderstanding, really. I didn't mean to scare anyone, I promise. 

But since then, I guess I've just kind of pulled back from everything. The coaching, the volunteering... I just stopped being around the people who used to count on me. I didn't want to cause any more trouble, you know? I figured it was better if I just kept to myself for a while until I got things sorted out. 

I'm really trying to get back on track, though. I want to get back to work and be dependable again. Does... does that make sense? I hope you don't think less of me because of the suspension. I really am a good worker.
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities is interfering with your daily life?

Well, um... I guess if you're asking about my daily life, it... it probably is interfering a bit. I mean, I really don't want to overstate it, but... 

Like I was saying about work... the suspension... that really changed my day-to-day. You know, I was on that routine patrol and... well, I guess I just wasn't acting like myself, and I ended up scaring some of the staff and the people around. It's so embarrassing to talk about. I really, really didn't mean to upset anyone, I swear. I'm usually the one keeping people safe, right? 

And since that happened, my daily routine just... stopped. I pulled away from the coaching, and the volunteering I used to do. I just felt like... maybe the people who used to count on me would be better off if I just stepped back for a bit. So I'm not doing much of anything right now. 

I know that probably sounds like I'm not handling things well, but I'm really trying to figure it all out so I can get back to normal. I just want to be helpful again. Is it okay that I took a step back from everything? I just didn't want to make things worse for anyone else.
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities and feelings of emptiness are significantly impacting your ability to function in your daily life?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm completely incapable of doing things, you know? I'm still trying my best. But... yeah, I suppose it is having a pretty big impact right now. 

I know I've mentioned it a couple of times already, and I'm really sorry to keep bringing it up, it's just... the suspension from work is probably the biggest thing. When I was on that patrol and... well, startled the staff and the bystanders... it just derailed everything. I'm so sorry if I sound like a broken record, I just... I really want you to understand that I wasn't trying to be a problem for anyone. 

But because of that, and just feeling so... empty, I guess... I really have pulled away from everything. The coaching, the volunteering... all the people who used to rely on me. I just felt like I needed to remove myself so I wouldn't mess anything else up. So, yeah, I guess my day-to-day functioning is pretty much on hold right now. 

I know that's not what you want to hear from a patient, and I promise I'm going to work hard to get back to where I was. I just need a little time to get my head straight. Do you think... do you think it's understandable that I'm struggling this much right now, given everything that happened?
